root_cause.text: The s390 BPF JIT’s trampoline marshalling code applied sign-extension only, so unsigned BTF-specified kfunc arguments and BPF program return values were passed/stored with the wrong upper bits, violating the s390x ABI.
root_cause.evidence: The patch replaces `sign_extend()` with `sign_zero_extend()` in `arch/s390/net/bpf_jit_comp.c`, and for sizes 1/2/4 adds zero-extending instructions (`llgcr`, `llghr`, `llgfr`) when `BTF_FMODEL_SIGNED_ARG` is not set; the commit message explicitly says “s390 BPF JIT currently implements only sign extension” and that s390x ABI requires zero-extension for unsigned arguments and return values.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch replaces `sign_extend()` with `sign_zero_extend()` in `arch/s390/net/bpf_jit_comp.c`, and for sizes 1/2/4 adds zero-extending instructions (`llgcr`, `llghr`, `llgfr`) when `BTF_FMODEL_SIGNED_ARG` is not set; the commit message explicitly says “s390 BPF JIT currently implements only sign extension” and that s390x ABI requires zero-extension for unsigned arguments and return values.

intent_record.intent_summary: Update the BPF JIT argument extension logic to correctly sign-extend signed values and zero-extend unsigned values for smaller-than-register types.
intent_record.what: The helper function was renamed from `sign_extend` to `sign_zero_extend`, the early return for non-signed arguments was removed, and each of the 1-, 2-, and 4-byte cases now conditionally emits either a sign-extending instruction when `BTF_FMODEL_SIGNED_ARG` is set or a zero-extending instruction when it is not. The 8-byte case remains unchanged and still returns 0.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the JIT now normalizes smaller argument sizes according to their signedness instead of only sign-extending signed arguments and doing nothing for unsigned ones. This ensures unsigned 1/2/4-byte values are explicitly zero-extended to the full register width, preventing stale upper bits from affecting subsequent execution.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use sign-or-zero extension when preparing JIT call arguments so values are extended correctly according to their metadata.
intent_record.what: In the argument setup loop inside bpf_jit_insn(), the call to sign_extend() was replaced with sign_zero_extend() for each argument register BPF_REG_1 + j, while keeping the same arg size and arg flags parameters.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the JIT now extends function arguments using sign-or-zero extension logic instead of always sign extension, which changes how argument values are materialized in registers and can prevent incorrect interpretation of unsigned arguments or flags-dependent extension behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use zero extension rather than sign extension when saving the BPF program return value in the trampoline JIT.
intent_record.what: In invoke_bpf_prog(), the code path that prepares a saved return value changed from calling sign_extend(jit, REG_2, m->ret_size, m->ret_flags) to calling sign_zero_extend(jit, REG_2, m->ret_size, m->ret_flags) before storing %r2 into the retval slot.
intent_record.how: This changes how the BPF program return value is normalized before being saved: instead of preserving the signed interpretation of smaller return types, the value is now zero-extended, which affects the runtime value written to retval_off and prevents unwanted sign propagation.

candidates.rationale: This conditional makes the helper return without extending values for unsigned arguments, so smaller-than-register unsigned kfunc arguments keep garbage upper bits instead of being zero-extended as required by the s390x ABI.
This early return is the point where unsigned arguments bypass any extension logic, causing the trampoline marshalling code to pass incorrect upper bits for unsigned BTF-specified parameters.
The call path unconditionally uses the sign-extension helper for kfunc arguments, which is the core mistake when the argument metadata indicates unsigned values that should be zero-extended.
The trampoline saves the BPF program return value using the sign-extension helper, which is wrong for return values that must be zero-extended before being stored according to the ABI.

vuln_statements.explanation: This call path applies the sign-extension helper when preparing trampoline call arguments. For unsigned BTF-described kfunc arguments, this causes the upper bits to be extended incorrectly instead of being zero-extended per the s390x ABI.
This statement stores the BPF program return value using sign extension. For return values that should be zero-extended, this preserves the wrong upper bits and violates the s390x ABI.
This condition identifies unsigned arguments, but the associated pre-fix logic does not perform the required zero-extension path for them, allowing incorrect upper bits to remain.
This early return lets unsigned arguments bypass any extension handling in the pre-fix code, which is the direct point where zero-extension should have occurred.
